info.name: classifier
info.description:
Document Classifier endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/classifier` → `http://classifier:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST/DELETE, `forward_headers: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/classifier/API.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Direct base URL (bypassing LiteLLM, only useful inside the ai_shared network or when PORT_CLASSIFIER is published): http://classifier:8000 or http://<host>:${PORT_CLASSIFIER}. All examples in this collection use the LiteLLM pass-through path.

Async-job pattern: POST /assess and POST /assess/compare both return 202 Accepted immediately with `{job_id, phase: "pending"}`. Callers poll GET /jobs/{job_id} until `phase` is `completed` or `failed`, then read the `result` field. Job tracking is powered by the shared `common.jobs` package (SqliteRegistry backend); the `/jobs`, `/jobs/{id}`, and DELETE `/jobs/{id}` routes are mounted via `common.jobs.router.build_router(..., include_delete=True, include_cancel=False)`. Response migration note: the top-level `id` is now `job_id`, `status` is now `phase`, and the previously separate `type` + `request_id` columns are nested under `metadata`. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}` for the full shape.

Copy the `job_id` from a POST /assess or POST /assess/compare response into the `jobId` collection variable to run the GET/DELETE /jobs/{jobId} requests.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the /v1/classifier pass-through — most keys created for chat models already do. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth, then forwarded to the classifier by LiteLLM because the pass-through has `forward_headers: true`.
job_id returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare. Fill in after submitting to run GET /jobs/{jobId} and DELETE /jobs/{jobId}. `phase` values progress pending → processing → completed | failed.

request.description: Liveness check used by the Docker healthcheck (`docker-compose.classifier.yml` → `healthcheck.test` hits /health every 30s) and by load balancers. Returns `{"status": "ok"}` with HTTP 200 whenever the FastAPI process is up. Does NOT probe the SQLite jobs registry, the vLLM backend, or the background worker — a stuck worker will still show `status: ok` here. Excluded from Prometheus instrumentation (see `Instrumentator(excluded_handlers=["/metrics", "/health"])` in main.py). See API.md § `GET /health`.

Enumerate all available `hint` values and their LLM scoring rubrics. Returns `{"hints": {"quality": {...}, "presence": {...}, "auto": {...}}}` where each rubric object has `heading`, `rubric`, and `extra` fields sourced from `llm.HINT_RUBRICS`. Use these values as the `hint` field on a CriterionInput:

- `quality`: score image quality 1-10 (1-3 = FAIL, 4-6 = MARGINAL, 7-10 = PASS).
- `presence`: detect presence/absence (10=present, 5=uncertain, 1=absent) with chain-of-thought reasoning in `extra`.
- `auto` (default): LLM infers the rubric from the criterion name.

No request body. See API.md § `GET /hints`.

List every registered OpenCV detector, grouped by underlying detector function. Returns `{"detectors": [{"function": "check_blur", "names": ["is blurry", "is sharp", "sharpness"]}, ...], "total_names": N}`. Use any of the `names` as the `name` field on a CriterionInput with `type="cv"` — fuzzy matching is applied at runtime, so near-matches also work. If no detector matches, the criterion silently falls back to LLM scoring and the response's `method` field reflects the actual path taken.

Built-in detector functions: `check_blur` (Laplacian variance), `check_exposure` (mean pixel intensity), `detect_vegetation` (HSV green masking), `detect_sky`, `detect_faces` (Haar cascade), `detect_water`, `detect_text` (Sobel edge density). See API.md § `Built-in cv detector names`.

formdata.description: JPEG or PNG image file. Read into memory during the request via `await image.read()`; the worker receives the bytes, so the UploadFile is not stored on disk.

formdata.value: [{"name":"has electrical meter","type":"llm","hint":"presence","weight":4.0},{"name":"meter value is readable","type":"llm","hint":"quality","weight":3.0,"depends_on":"has electrical meter"},{"name":"three feet of clearance around meter","type":"llm","hint":"presence","weight":2.5,"depends_on":"has electrical meter"},{"name":"sharpness","type":"cv","weight":1.0}]
formdata.description: JSON array of CriterionInput objects. Each must have `name`; optional fields are `type` (`llm` default | `cv`), `weight` (float > 0, default 1.0), `hint` (`quality` | `presence` | `auto` default), and `depends_on` (name of another criterion that must PASS score >= 7 before this one runs — otherwise this criterion is marked SKIPPED and excluded from the weighted score). Chains are supported: A → B → C all skip if A fails. If omitted, `config.DEFAULT_CRITERIA` is used.

request.description:
Submit a single-image assessment job. Content-Type is `multipart/form-data`. Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{"job_id": "<id>", "phase": "pending"}` — this is the async pattern, so poll GET /jobs/{jobId} until `phase` is `completed` or `failed`, then read the `result` field.

Server-side flow (main.py `assess_document`):
  1. Parse the `criteria` JSON form field via `analysis.parse_criteria`.
  2. Read the uploaded image bytes into memory (UploadFile is only readable during the request).
  3. Create a job record in the SQLite jobs registry with `metadata={type: "assess", request_id: <req>}` and `initial_phase="pending"`.
  4. Enqueue `(job_id, "assess", {image_bytes, content_type, filename, criteria}, req_id)` into `workers.job_queue`.
  5. Return `202` with the job_id.

Errors: **400** if the criteria list is empty or the image body is empty; **422** if the criteria JSON is malformed or fails Pydantic validation of CriterionInput.

Result shape once completed: `{image_info, assessment: {overall_verdict, overall_score, per_criterion_scores, weighted_score_breakdown}, verdict}`. SKIPPED criteria appear in `per_criterion_scores` with `verdict: "SKIPPED"`, `score: null`, `method: "skipped"`, and a reason string, and are excluded from the weighted score. See API.md § `POST /assess`.

Postman note: click the `image` row's file selector to attach a real JPEG/PNG — the placeholder `src` in this template is empty.

Submit a comparison job — assess a subject image against one or more reference examples. Content-Type is `application/json`. Body is a CompareRequest (see models.py):

- `image`: ImageInput `{data, type: "base64" | "url"}`. URL inputs are SSRF-checked before fetching (see ssrf.py).
- `criteria`: list[CriterionInput], defaults to `config.DEFAULT_CRITERIA` if omitted.
- `aggregation`: `mean` (default, balanced) | `min` (strictest — must match all examples) | `max` (most lenient — must match any).
- `examples`: list[ExampleInput] with `min_length=1`. Each has `data`, `type`, `weight` (0.0–1.0, default 0.5 — how much similarity to this example influences the combined score; `0.0` = ignore, `1.0` = similarity only), and optional `pre_generated_analysis` (a prior `result` from /assess to skip re-analysing the reference).

Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{"job_id": "<id>", "phase": "pending"}`. Poll GET /jobs/{jobId} for the result.

Server-side flow (main.py `assess_with_reference`):
  1. Validate `request.criteria` non-empty (Pydantic already enforces `examples` min_length=1).
  2. Create a job record with `metadata={type: "compare", request_id: <req>}`.
  3. Enqueue the full CompareRequest object into `workers.job_queue` — workers._run_compare receives it directly, no re-parsing.
  4. Return `202` with the job_id.

Errors: **400** if criteria list is empty; **422** if the body fails CompareRequest validation (missing examples, invalid aggregation literal, weight out of range, malformed ImageInput/ExampleInput).

Combined-score formula: `combined = (1 - weight) × input_overall_score + weight × similarity_score`. Result shape: `{status, criteria, aggregation, input_analysis, example_results[], aggregate: {method, combined_score, combined_verdict, per_example_combined_scores}}`. See API.md § `POST /assess/compare`.

Caching: `pre_generated_analysis` values must come from the SAME version of the classifier that is currently running — stored analyses from older versions cause runtime errors. Re-generate after upgrades. See API.md § Caching example analyses.

List recent jobs, newest first. Mounted by `common.jobs.router.build_router(jobs_registry, include_delete=True, include_cancel=False)` in main.py; backed by `SqliteRegistry.list_all()`. Returns a JobsListResponse — see `shared/common/src/common/jobs/model.py` for the JobBase shape. Result blobs are excluded from the list response (call GET /jobs/{job_id} to get the full `result` field).

Each job's `metadata` is the ClassifierMetadata blob `{type: "assess" | "compare", request_id: <req>}` written at submit time — useful for filtering by kind or correlating with the `[request_id]` in server logs (see middleware.py's CorrelationIDMiddleware). See API.md § `GET /jobs`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare.

request.description:
Poll for the status and result of a submitted job. Set the `jobId` collection variable to the `job_id` returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare first.

Response shape (JobBase from `common.jobs`):
  `{job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata: {type, request_id}, result, error}`

`phase` progression: `pending` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`.

- While `pending` / `processing`: `result` is null, `error` is null. Keep polling.
- When `completed`: `result` is the assessment (see POST /assess or POST /assess/compare descriptions for the exact shape).
- When `failed`: `error` holds the exception message set by the worker via `jobs_registry.set_error(...)`, `result` is null.

Errors: **404** if the `job_id` is unknown (registry.get returned None). Note the response migration: top-level `id` is now `job_id`, `status` is now `phase`, and the previously separate `type` + `request_id` columns are nested under `metadata`. Callers that parse the response by field name need to update accordingly. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare.

request.description:
Delete a job record from the SQLite registry. Returns **204 No Content** on success (empty body). Idempotent from the caller's perspective in the sense that once gone the record stays gone — but the underlying `registry.delete` returns False for unknown ids, so a repeat call for the same id returns **404** with `detail: "no job '<id>'"`.

No cancel semantics: the worker doesn't currently observe a cancel signal mid-analysis, so `include_cancel=False` on the mounted router (see main.py). Deleting a job that's still `pending` / `processing` removes the record from the DB but does NOT abort the in-flight worker task — the worker will attempt to write its result/error to a row that no longer exists (logged, but harmless). See API.md § `DELETE /jobs/{job_id}`.
